historicalReferences: Think back to 1994, when Nigel Mansell delivered that stunning victory, his final F1 win, right here in Adelaide.
Damon Hill's controversial collision with Michael Schumacher in '94, right at turn six, a moment forever etched in F1 history.
The 1986 finale, where Mansell's tyre exploded on the Brabham Straight, handing the title to Alain Prost, a heart-stopping moment for the Brit!
Remember 1991, when Ayrton Senna secured his third and final World Championship at this very circuit, a moment of pure brilliance.
The circuit has seen some incredible battles over the years, with legends like Prost, Senna, and Mansell all fighting for glory.
The Adelaide circuit was known for its demanding nature, testing both driver and machine to their absolute limits.
Many say Adelaide was the true test of driving skill back in the day, a proper old-school street circuit.
The 1985 Australian Grand Prix saw Keke Rosberg take victory in his Williams, a fitting end to his Formula One career.
The first ever Formula 1 race here in 1985, a landmark event for Australian motorsport.
The narrow confines of this track have always encouraged daring overtakes and dramatic moments, adding to its legendary status.

strategyPoints: Tire wear will be a critical factor on this abrasive surface, especially on the left-hand side. Expect to see some interesting strategy calls.
With a relatively short pit lane, the pit window will be open for a significant portion of the race. The undercut could be very powerful.
Fuel management will be key, especially in the closing stages. The drivers will need to balance pace with conserving fuel.
The 3.78km lap length means we'll see plenty of action, with opportunities for multiple pit stops and strategic variations.
The narrow track layout makes overtaking difficult, so track position is paramount. Qualifying will be crucial.
A safety car is always a possibility on a street circuit like Adelaide, so teams need to be prepared to react quickly.
The high-speed nature of the circuit puts a lot of stress on the tires, so teams will need to carefully monitor their performance.
With limited run-off areas, any mistake will be severely punished, making consistency and precision essential for a strong result.
